title: Accepted-Window Runtime Lineage and Crop-Event Delivery Seam
goal: Implement the smallest runtime-owned lineage seam that can collect IQROT/IPTRA-equivalent process integrals during a physical trial, admit them to one WOFOST crop window only after an F-KT commit has actually advanced the same lineage/revision/interval, freeze a complete accepted aggregate carrier for F-WOF33, and prevent more than one successfully committed crop-event delivery for that window.

constructor_inputs: F-KT kernel_checkpoint_t captured before the interval
F-KT kernel_committed_state_t observed after a successful commit
required_proof: checkpoint and committed state are ready and share the same positive lineage
committed revision equals checkpoint origin revision + 1
committed post-time is strictly after checkpoint time
accepted_interval_certificate.forgery_boundary: certificate components are private and there is no public constructor from an accepted boolean or caller-supplied revision pair
accepted_interval_certificate.meaning: F-KT has published exactly one continuation interval on this lineage between the checkpoint time and the committed post-time

trial_contribution.ownership: worker/job-local scratch; never committed column state
trial_contribution.seed: same F-KT checkpoint provenance as the candidate trial
trial_contribution.accumulation: for each process subinterval, IQROT-equivalent integral += actual_root_uptake_rate * dt and IPTRA-equivalent integral += potential_transpiration_rate * dt
requirements: subintervals contiguous and wholly inside the trial interval
first subinterval starts at trial t0 and complete contribution ends at trial t1 before admission
trial_contribution.discard: discarding/replacing a trial contribution cannot modify any accepted-window total

accepted_window.seed: F-KT checkpoint at crop-window t0 plus explicit generic window t1
accepted_window.admission: trial contribution enters totals only when certificate lineage, origin revision and exact interval match the trial, and certificate origin revision equals the window next expected revision
accepted_window.coverage: accepted intervals must be contiguous, non-overlapping and cannot pass the crop-window t1
accepted_window.complete: coverage end equals crop-window t1 within qualified time tolerance
accepted_window.rejected_trial_zero_contribution: proven by mutation tests in which rejected/discarded trial contributions contain nonzero values but window totals remain unchanged

crop_event_delivery.prepare: a complete accepted window may produce a private provenance-bound event token plus a frozen aggregate carrier; preparation is read-only and repeatable for crop retry
crop_event_delivery.commit_delivery: after the runtime has successfully committed the corresponding crop candidate, the token may mark the window delivered exactly once
crop_event_delivery.retry_before_delivery_commit: same complete window returns bitwise identical token/aggregates
crop_event_delivery.calendar_scheduler: not implemented; the runtime event condition is generic window completion rather than midnight

qualified_semantic_producer_relationship.actual_root_uptake: root_water_uptake_flux_result_t.actual_uptake_total exists for the qualified root-water-uptake process
qualified_semantic_producer_relationship.potential_transpiration: qualified ET/crop-root seams expose potential_transpiration as a current-process quantity
qualified_semantic_producer_relationship.reason: F-WOF34 qualifies lineage/aggregation/delivery semantics; actual production process calls must be bound where the corresponding trial process outputs are already available, not invented by this seam

not_qualified: actual Richards/root-uptake/ET production binding that invokes trial accumulation at every accepted physical process substep
full runtime ownership/lifetime of active crop-window metadata across restart or distributed execution
full historical multi-day B1.10 crop trajectory equivalence
IDSL=2, SWRD=2/3, nutrients, potential crop trajectory, soybean or grass
